podcasts.name: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Founding (1981)
podcast.body: Victor Tsoy and guitarist Alex S. Rybin founded their first band, Garin i Giperboloidy, in June 1981, before eventually changing its name to Kino. "Punto, en vez de a uno de 1961, fundaron su propia banda, Gary Nighy pervolo Di."

srcs.episode: Viktor Tsoi. El padre del Postpunk Ruso

podcast.title: Name Change (1982)
podcast.body: The band Garin i Giperboloidy changed its name to Kino in 1982, establishing the identity under which they would become renowned. "Y ya, en 1982, se cambiaron el nombre áquino."

srcs.episode: Viktor Tsoi. El padre del Postpunk Ruso

podcast.title: Internal Conflict and Lineup Change (Post-45)
podcast.body: Following their debut album, Kino experienced a challenging period marked by creative differences between Victor Tsoy and Alex S. Rybin. Their clashing ideas regarding the group's direction and leadership ultimately led to Rybin abandoning Kino, leaving Tsoy to continue the band alone. "Soy Ribin Chocaban y tenía ni ideas contraria sobre el rumbo y el liderazgo del grupo, por lo que Ribin acabó abandonando Quinoa."

srcs.episode: Viktor Tsoi. El padre del Postpunk Ruso

podcast.title: Musical Evolution and Influences
podcast.body: For their subsequent albums, Kino expanded their lineup by recruiting more musicians and increasingly incorporated electronic instruments into their sound. Musically, they were considered close to bands like The Cure and Joy Division, and Victor Tsoy particularly admired The Smiths. Their distinctive dark and danceable sound was notably filtered by the brutalist architecture, coldness, and crudeness of Leningrad, creating a unique sonic identity that has since been embraced by the new wave of post-punk in Eastern Europe. "Posicalmente, que no estaba cerca de bandas como de Kyu, Royo y División, una de las bandas que más amigaba Victor Toy eran desmits."

srcs.episode: Viktor Tsoi. El padre del Postpunk Ruso

podcast.title: Rebirth on the Internet
podcast.body: Decades after their initial success, Kino has experienced a significant rebirth on the internet. Hundreds of their songs have been translated into Spanish and numerous other languages by young people who, despite the time difference, feel a deep connection with the band's music, demonstrating its timeless appeal. "seguramente sea por eso que Quinoa ha vivido un renacimiento en internet. De escenas de canciones suyas han sido traducidas al español y muchos otros idiomas por jóvenes que deca las despues, sin tener una profunda conexión con la banda."
